subject: ventures/dns-configuration-evidence
professional: a senior DNS operations engineer at an MSP who runs nameserver and mail cutovers for customers; first checks: is the DNS wire parsing right (RFC 1035 rdata, name compression, TXT string concatenation, TC-bit TCP fallback), are RCODEs kept apart (NXDOMAIN vs NODATA vs SERVFAIL/REFUSED, RFC 2308), is a CNAME never recorded as the requested type, is a failed lookup never reported as 'unchanged', does the authorization scope guard hold (evil-example.test is not inside example.test), and do the browser and CLI records really interoperate as claimed

evidence.correctness: Recomputed against dnspython 2.9.2 (an independent DNS library, installed in a scratch venv) and RFC 1035/7208 by hand. scratchpad wire_check.py builds responses with dnspython and feeds them to capture.parse_response: A via a CNAME chain -> ['192.0.2.7','192.0.2.8'] (dnspython: same), AAAA 2001:db8::1, NS x2, MX '10 mx1.example.test','20 mx2...' (correct; case differs only by dnspython's case-insensitive compression), TXT multi-string '"v=DKIM1; k=rsa; " "p=MIIBIjAN"' -> 'v=DKIM1; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjAN' (correct per RFC 7208 3.3 concatenation), null MX '0 .', REFUSED -> refused, SERVFAIL -> error, NXDOMAIN -> []. End to end: a dnspython UDP+TCP server on 127.0.0.2:53 (scratchpad server.py) and `python3 -m dns_evidence capture --resolver 127.0.0.2`: A, MX, and a 40-record TXT set larger than 512 bytes all captured (UDP TC=1 -> TCP fallback works). Compare: examples/before.json vs after.json -> changed 1 (A 192.0.2.10 -> .11), unchanged 1 (TXT), matching a hand diff; journey (stubbed DoH, Playwright) counts changed 1 / unchanged 3 / inconclusive 2 as its scenario dictates. Errors found: (1) the CLI records an A query on a dangling CNAME as answers ['CNAME gone.cdn.test'] (dnspython: no A in the answer; the browser records []), so the CLI writes a CNAME into an A row; (2) the browser normalises an RFC 7505 null MX '0 .' to '0 ' (shown in the page as '0 '); (3) the browser collapses whitespace inside TXT strings ('"two  spaces"' -> 'two spaces'), so a real whitespace change reports unchanged; (4) both record NXDOMAIN and NOERROR/NODATA identically as []; (5) the Python compare treats a string `answers` value as a list of characters ('192.0.2.1' -> 9 one-character answers, reported 'changed') where the JS rejects it. Not 4: these are edge cases, but (1) and (4) sit exactly where a cutover goes wrong (dangling CNAMEs, deleted names).
evidence.completeness: README/page features checked: browser capture over three DoH endpoints with per-resolver rows, authorization tick, out-of-domain refusal, unknown-type refusal, save baseline, load baseline/file, compare, Markdown copy, JSON download, saved-baseline prefill: all pass in tests/journey.mjs (23 PASS lines, run with PLAYWRIGHT=$(npm root -g)/playwright/index.js) and my own Playwright run. CLI capture (plan file and flags, --authorized required, out-of-domain exit 1, timeout recorded as status 'timeout'), compare json/markdown, --fail-on changed (exit 2), legacy `python3 -m dns_evidence.cli` form: all work. Gaps: the browser offers SOA, CAA, SRV, PTR (and @ CAA is in the default list) while the CLI rejects CAA ('unsupported query type'); 'a baseline captured in the browser compares with python3 -m dns_evidence compare, and vice versa' loads but cannot compare, because the browser stores resolver ids 'cloudflare'/'google'/'quad9' and the CLI stores the IP it was given, so every row is inconclusive. No stubs or TODOs; live DoH endpoints and the served page could not be reached from this sandbox (proxy 403).
evidence.verification: `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`: 31 tests OK in 0.013 s. `node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 47 pass, 0 fail, 126 ms, including a parity test that runs the Python CLI and diffs Markdown byte for byte (python3 present, so it ran, not skipped). tests/journey.mjs: 23 checks pass but it is not in CI and does not resolve a global Playwright without the PLAYWRIGHT env var. Seeded 10 mutants with quality_mutate.py: 6 caught (JS scope guard, RCODE 5->4, JS NXDOMAIN-as-error, JS type filter, query-id check removed, JS HTTP error -> empty answers), 4 survived: Python authorization guard `endswith('.' + apex)` -> `endswith(apex)` (evil-example.test accepted), Python report `status in UNCERTAIN` -> `== 'timeout'` (a refused/error observation then compares as unchanged, the product's core promise), parse_response `typed if typed else others` -> `typed`, TC-bit mask 0x0200 -> 0x0100. No test exercises the UDP/TCP transport.
evidence.craft: Read dns-evidence.mjs (381 lines), capture.py (417), report.py (128), cli.py (162), index.html script, test files. Strengths: one pure JS engine imported by the page, DNS text only reaches the DOM via textContent, atomic writes, bounded plan sizes and timeouts, compression-loop guard, a real parity test between the two implementations. Defects: parse_response accepts any reply with the right ID without checking QR or that the question matches (a response for evil.test was accepted as the answer for example.test; a QR=0 echo became an empty successful answer); the Python compare crashes with a traceback (exit 1) on `answers: null` or a missing file instead of a message; Python load_snapshot does not check `answers` is a list (JS does), so the two validators disagree; the compare exit code 2 for --fail-on is the same as argparse's usage-error exit 2; journey.mjs not in CI. Two engines in two languages is a deliberate, tested choice.
evidence.claims: Checked 9 claims. Backed: never folds a failed lookup into unchanged (journey + my compare run, JS side), nothing uploaded (Playwright saw only same-origin files plus the three DoH hosts), scope boundary enforced in the browser (FQDN outside the domain refused), TC/TCP and statuses stored as timeout/refused/error (local server run), no-warranty disclaimer on every page, served llms.txt carries marisstella.app URLs (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder left). Not backed: (1) README.md:22-24 and the FAQ (index.html:181 and FAQPage schema) say browser and CLI snapshots compare 'vice versa' and 'The two produce the same report', and the caveat (README.md:36, index.html:189) says mixing can show a 'cosmetic changed'; in fact resolver identities never match (cloudflare vs 1.1.1.1), so a mixed compare reports every row inconclusive (ran it: 0 changed, 0 unchanged, 4 inconclusive); (2) the propagation page answers 'Can I make a change go faster once made?' with 'No' (how-long-does-dns-propagation-take.html:67), ignoring the public cache-purge tools Cloudflare (1.1.1.1 purge cache) and Google Public DNS (flush cache) offer for exactly the resolvers this tool queries; (3) the dig comparison says dig shows a timeout as 'an answer section with nothing in it' (vs-checking-dns-by-hand.html:72,93), while dig prints ';; connection timed out' and a status line; (4) llms.txt:5 says 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', boilerplate that does not describe a DNS observation tool.
evidence.fitness: Walked the MSP job: before a mail cutover, enter the domain, tick authorization, capture A/MX/TXT/NS/_dmarc over three resolvers, save baseline, change records, recapture, build report, paste Markdown into the ticket. With stubbed DoH this works end to end in Chromium and the Markdown carries per-resolver before/after answers and timestamps; a practitioner could hand it to a customer. Gaps a senior DNS engineer hits in the first hour: no TTL recorded (stated honestly in the FAQ), NXDOMAIN and NODATA look the same ('no records'), the browser cannot ask the authoritative nameservers (the most direct evidence a change was published; the CLI can by naming their IPs, but the README does not suggest it), CDN- or geo-balanced names (the default 'www A') will report 'changed' between captures with no zone change and the page does not warn, the DNSSEC AD flag is captured in the browser but never shown or compared, and mixing browser and CLI captures yields an all-inconclusive report.
evidence.domain: Compared against RFC 1035 (message format, compression, TC bit), RFC 2308 (negative answers), RFC 5452 section 9.1 (match the question section), RFC 7208 3.3 (TXT concatenation) and RFC 7505 (null MX), and common practice (dig output). Matches: wire parsing and rdata rendering for the six CLI types, TCP fallback on truncation, random 16-bit query IDs, RCODE 5 as refused and other non-0/3 RCODEs as error, TXT strings concatenated, a failed lookup kept apart from an empty answer. Departures: NXDOMAIN (name gone) and NODATA (type gone) are recorded identically, losing the distinction RFC 2308 draws and dig shows; the question section and QR bit of a reply are not checked; the CLI writes a dangling CNAME into an A row as 'CNAME target' while the browser drops it, so the same zone yields different evidence by interface; null MX is mangled in the browser; TXT inner whitespace is collapsed; no EDNS0 and no TTL. The propagation article is right on the mechanism (TTL-bounded caches, TLD delegation TTLs of two days for .com explaining '24-48 hours', lower TTL in advance) but omits negative caching of a name queried before it existed and the resolver purge tools.

mutations.change: return host == apex or host.endswith("." + apex) -> return host == apex or host.endswith(apex)
return n === d || n.endsWith(`.${d}`); -> return n === d || n.endsWith(d);
return typed if typed else others -> return typed
if observation.get("status") in UNCERTAIN: -> if observation.get("status") == "timeout":

defects.what: Tests miss two guards the product is built on: in the Python engine, weakening the authorization scope check to endswith(apex) (so evil-example.test passes for example.test) survives, and narrowing report.py's UNCERTAIN check to 'timeout' only (so a refused or error observation compares as unchanged) survives; the TC-bit TCP fallback and the CNAME fallback in parse_response are also untested (4 of 10 mutants survive)

README and page FAQ claim browser and CLI snapshots compare 'vice versa' and 'produce the same report', warning only of a cosmetic 'changed'; resolver identities differ (browser 'cloudflare'/'google'/'quad9', CLI the IP it was given), so a mixed compare reports every row inconclusive

CLI records an A/AAAA/MX query whose answer holds only a CNAME (e.g. a dangling CNAME) as answers ['CNAME target'], writing a CNAME into the requested-type row; the browser records [] for the same zone, so the evidence differs by interface
NXDOMAIN and NOERROR/NODATA are both recorded as an empty answer list, so a deleted name and a deleted record type are indistinguishable in the evidence (RFC 2308; dig shows the status)

parse_response accepts any reply with the right ID: it checks neither the QR bit nor that the question matches (RFC 5452 9.1); a reply for evil.test A was accepted as the answer for example.test, and a QR=0 echo became an empty successful answer
Browser normalises an RFC 7505 null MX '0 .' to '0 ' (shown on the page and in the report), and the CLI keeps '0 .'
Browser collapses runs of whitespace inside TXT strings before comparing, so a TXT value that changed only in internal whitespace reports unchanged; escaped quotes inside chunks are kept escaped

Python load_snapshot does not require answers to be a list: a string is split into characters and reported 'changed'; answers null crashes with a TypeError traceback (exit 1). The JS validator rejects both
Browser offers SOA, CAA, SRV, PTR (CAA in the default list) while the CLI rejects them, and the page does not say the types are browser-only

Propagation page says nothing can make a change land faster once made, omitting the public cache-purge tools of Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 and Google Public DNS (the resolvers this tool queries) and negative caching of names queried before they existed
Comparison page says dig shows a timeout as 'an answer section with nothing in it'; dig prints ';; connection timed out' (and a status line for REFUSED/SERVFAIL)
llms.txt carries generic boilerplate 'Results are estimates from the numbers typed in', which does not describe a DNS observation recorder

The browser journey test is not in CI and fails with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND unless PLAYWRIGHT points at a Playwright entry file; the DNSSEC AD flag is captured in browser snapshots but never shown or compared

verdict: A carefully built before/after DNS evidence recorder with a browser (DoH) and a Python (wire protocol) front end. The core is right where I could check it independently: the RFC 1035 parser agrees with dnspython on A, AAAA, NS, MX and multi-string TXT, truncated replies fall back to TCP against a real local server, the shipped examples diff correctly, and the Playwright journey passes 23 checks with failed lookups kept as inconclusive. It misses the bar on verification and claims. 4 of 10 seeded bugs survive, including weakening the Python authorization-scope guard and letting refused/error lookups compare as unchanged, which is the product's central promise. The README and FAQ say browser and CLI snapshots compare both ways, but resolver ids never match, so every mixed row is inconclusive. A DNS engineer would also hit NXDOMAIN and NODATA recorded identically, a dangling CNAME written into an A row by the CLI (the browser drops it), null MX mangled in the browser, and no TTL. Finished for the browser workflow it describes; not yet at senior DNS-operations sign-off.
